title: A Candid Threat
text: Ah, so she'd noticed after all. Well, that was only to be expected from Older Sister. So I smoothly released my concealment and emerged from the shadows, as if stepping out of darkness itself. That said, I kept my hood pulled down low, not yet ready to reveal my true face.
“Oh my, you really were here—I had a feeling you might be.”
“I intended to speak with you from the start, I say.”
“Oh my, oh my… and what business might you have with me?”

Her tone was casual, but her wariness was at an extremely high level—something I could tell just from knowing Older Sister through all these loops. The proof was that her usual cheerful “Big Sister” self-reference had vanished entirely. How best to answer, I wondered. I’d considered this in advance, but let’s go with the approach most likely to succeed.
“Well now… this will sound like absolute nonsense, but to put it bluntly, I’d like you not to go out fishing in the open sea, indeed.”

I answered as sincerely as possible, keeping things peaceable and mixing in almost no falsehoods. Older Sister was remarkably skilled at seeing through acting, so I judged that honesty would land better than lies.
“And why might that be?”
“A future awaits in which you regret it to the point of death… though saying it like that makes it sound like a threat. To be frank, it was me who sank the ships of the village and the town.”
“I rather suspected as much. So why did you do such a thing, I wonder—care to tell me?”
“Does Older Sister know of the disaster called the Waves?”
“A tsunami… perhaps?”
Just as I thought—without facing it directly, it seemed the old legends alone didn’t quite click.
“It’s the prophecy spoken of in this world—the event called the Waves of Calamity, a crisis for the whole world, I say.”
“Oh my, is that so.”
“Indeed.”
“And what of it?”
“In roughly three days—no, we’ve already crossed into two—it will strike this region. And at the same time, the sea will grow violent, raging beyond reason because of the Wave’s influence.”
Older Sister blinked several times as she listened to me. There was no mistaking that look—What on earth is this man saying?
“And just as the prophecy foretells, monsters will spill forth from the Wave and attack the people of this region, claiming a great many victims, I say.”

Even I only knew of the Waves before summoning through hearsay, and only about this village and town as the sites struck. I’d heard what kind of monsters appeared, though. I believed they matched the monsters from the game’s knowledge.
“How dreadful.”

“And if Older Sister goes out fishing, won’t you be caught right in the middle of it? Along with everyone who goes out with you, people dear to you will perish, and you’ll come to regret it most terribly.”
“Oh myyy.”
Her reaction was a touch weak—no, more a look of disbelief, I’d say. Of course, I wasn’t one to be discouraged by something so minor.
“It seems Older Sister has people who are very dear to her. So, in order to protect them, I’ve come to honestly ask that you not go out fishing, I say.”
“Hmm… now what should I do, I wonder.”
“Of course, I’ll apologize for destroying the ships. And once this is all over, I’ll see to proper compensation as well.”
“And what if Big Sister here decided to simply capture you instead?”
“Could you manage that, I wonder?”
In a flash, she raised her harpoon with one hand, so I drew my spear and took my stance as well.

We circled, shuffling our feet, locking eyes. I found myself wondering—was Older Sister truly just an ordinary fisherwoman? Her skill was far too sharp for that, stronger than any average adventurer or mercenary. Something was clearly going on with her, though I hadn’t the faintest idea what.
“You’re quite the handful, aren’t you.”
“A compliment, I say.”

In an instant, Older Sister seemed to have sensed my true strength. At least at this point in the loop, she hadn’t yet broken her level limit, so she was only around level 40—though even then, her stats were formidable.
“Saying you don’t want me to go fishing is all well and good, but Big Sister has her own circumstances to consider, you know?”
“Éclair’s parent… Seaetto, wasn’t it? I believe her position within Melromarc was said to be precarious.”
“That’s right. It seems things get rather dire if she can’t bring back the fish.”

“Isn’t there still some time to spare on that matter? The… Cri—the princess, I mean, still has time before her return, so there should be ample leeway. In the first place, is there truly a fixed deadline for bringing back the fish in question?”
“They’re living creatures, so it’s not quite that strictly decided.”

As for the Crimson Swine’s return, it wasn’t happening at all in any loop, so the leeway was essentially infinite, I say. Besides, once the Wave struck, that would hardly matter anymore. In all likelihood, this fish-gathering errand had never once succeeded in any loop.
“Then surely it wouldn’t be so difficult to find some excuse to delay by another two days or so?”
“Such as?”
“Well now. Perhaps Older Sister could have a drink before departure and forcibly get every last fisherman hopelessly hungover, thereby postponing the trip to a later day, I say.”
For Older Sister, that would surely be child’s play. She was more than capable of drinking an entire crew under the table.
“Oh myyy… so you want me to go and do the very thing I’ve been holding myself back from, hm?”
That reaction didn’t sit well with me. Precisely because I knew Older Sister’s character to some degree.

“I suspect those around you would try to stop you, but if you simply kept drinking, and then said right before departure that you were feeling too hungover to go, I imagine you could buy a fair amount of time that way.”
“If I did something like that, Big Sister would get scolded somethinawful.”
She said it playfully, feigning mischief, but her eyes weren’t smiling at all. …As I suspected, negotiations without Father present were a difficult business. Time to hint at the second stage.
“…I’ve gone into this negotiation fully expecting not to be believed. So I’m well aware that, in essence, this amounts to a warning—nearly an order, I say.”
“And what will you do if I don’t comply?”

In a flash, I closed the distance into Older Sister’s range in an instant and thrust my spear right up to her face. The way her body instinctively arched back told me plenty—despite the level difference, she truly was a formidable expert. Her eyes narrowed into a sharp, glaring look as she tried to put distance between us, but she couldn’t keep pace with my speed. Of course, this was merely a warning.
“Do you understand now, I wonder? This is a warning, I say.”
“……Oh myyy.”
Older Sister fell into thought, clearly pondering what to do.

“The poison laced into this spear will simply put you to sleep until the appointed time comes… Ah, of course, you’re welcome to pretend to believe me and report this to the villagers if you like. Should that happen, I’ll simply have to treat the villagers—no, everyone in this entire territory—the very same way.”
With my power, it would certainly cause quite the commotion, but it wasn’t beyond doing. My strength as a Hero was that formidable, after all.
“Would you care to tell me why you’d go so far?”

Her wariness raised to its absolute peak, Older Sister asked. Her expression said she couldn’t believe me, yet still wanted to know the reason. Across all these loops, honestly telling someone I’d come from the future before the incident occurred had never once succeeded. That I’d come from the future was, I supposed, simply too hard to believe—but I had no choice but to say it regardless.
“I know you won’t believe me just because I say I’ve come from the future, but I’ll say it all the same, I say. I have come from the future.”
“Oh myyy… then just who exactly are you, I wonder? No, wait. Carrying that spear, being so much stronger than Big Sister—could it be you’re one of the Legendary Heroes?”
“I won’t deny it, I say.”
With the spear still leveled at her, Older Sister kept her wary eyes fixed on me.

“In the future, Older Sister kept regretting this terribly, over and over. If only she’d been there, in that place, at that time… By good fortune, I was granted that very chance, which is why I stand here now, obstructing you, I say.”
Our gazes remained locked, unbroken, for a long moment. Despite her large build, pinning Older Sister down would be simple enough.
“You, it seems… are not someone Big Sister can handle.”
As if in surrender, Older Sister raised both hands. That said, I couldn’t afford to let my guard down. After all, being reluctant to give up easily was also very much a part of who Older Sister was.
